about: Task 16c's zone extracts on Net3, a public network with two entry points (its reservoirs River and Lake), simulated only (R6): each inlet dosed at its own share of the dose, the superposition of the two inlets at one member (kb 0.40 per day, kw 0.70 m/day, the truth's default and off the grid's kw axis; a member on the grid added after the scored run) against the pre-registered bars (part 'superposition'), ratios (1, 1) as today's path (part 'identity'), leave-sites-out validation on a synthetic fixed route of 10 taps, with each group fit's training size (part 'holdout'), and an online analyzer at a zone inlet read as a boundary condition, not data, with the review's cases of declared inlets (part 'analyzer', invented readings). Written by python -m residualmap.intake_exp zone; the task16c checks in residualmap/checks.py rerun every part and compare.

superposition.units_note: the grid writes each dose to EPANET in the model's units, a thousand times its mg/L, so the file's tolerance of 0.01 is 1e-5 mg/L in the grid's units

on_grid_member.why: the scored member's kw (0.70 m/day, the truth's default) is not on the grid's kw axis; this member is on every free-chlorine grid; added after the scored run, which stands as scored

effect.what: this member with Lake's residual half River's, against every inlet at the one dose (today's path), daily means at each junction

analyzer.note: 1 tap the tap map marks as a zone inlet (AN-1 at Lake): its 2,880 usable readings are kept apart to set the inlet's residual and never fitted.

refused.inlet_missing: The model has 2 entry points (River, Lake) and 1 of them has no residual: Lake. Give every inlet's measured residual, or none.
refused.not_an_entry_point: Inlet Tank9 is not where water enters this model. Its entry points are River, Lake: give each inlet's residual under its node ID in the model.
refused.below_detection: The inlet residuals file has 1 row that cannot be used: row 3 (Lake: '<0.02'). Each row needs an inlet's node ID and its measured residual as a number in mg/L (a reading below detection cannot set an inlet's residual).
refused.given_twice: Inlet Lake has a residual in the inlet residuals file and readings at a tap the tap map marks as that inlet. Keep one of the two for each inlet.

outside_window.app_window_refused: Zone inlet Lake (tap INL) has no usable reading in the months the map is fitted on (2026-04, 2026-05, 2026-06) to set its residual: its 3 readings are dated 2026-01-10 to 2026-03-10. Every inlet needs a residual, or none: add usable readings of the inlet taps in those months, or give the inlet's residual in an inlet residuals file and clear the tap's role in the tap map.
outside_window.note: 1 tap the tap map marks as a zone inlet (INL at Lake): its 3 usable readings are kept apart to set the inlet's residual and never fitted.

only_below_detection.refused: Zone inlet Lake (tap INL) has no usable reading to set its residual: 3 readings cannot be used (below detection, not a number or above 10 mg/L; row 2: '<0.02', row 3: 'ND', row 4: '<0.02'). Every inlet needs a residual, or none: add usable readings of the inlet taps, or give the inlet's residual in an inlet residuals file and clear the tap's role in the tap map.
only_below_detection.note: 1 tap the tap map marks as a zone inlet (INL at Lake): no reading of it can set the inlet's residual (3 cannot: below detection, not a number or above 10 mg/L, listed as not used), and none is fitted.

roles_that_mark_no_inlet.warning: 3 taps of the tap map have roles that mention an inlet but do not mark a zone inlet (T1: 'not inlet', T2: 'non-inlet', INL: 'downstream of inlet'), so their readings are read as a tap's. A zone inlet's role is 'inlet' (or 'zone inlet', 'inlet analyzer', 'inlet tap').

review.inlet_at_a_junction_refused: The tap map marks tap INL (role 'Zone inlet') as a zone inlet at 20, which is not where water enters this model. Its entry points are River, Lake: a zone inlet tap's junction column names the entry point it measures, and a tap that is no zone inlet needs another role.

files_refused.thousands_separator_ugl: The inlet residuals file's residual column, 'residual_ugL', is in µg/L, and 1 residual is under 10 µg/L: row 2 (River: '1,200', 0.0012 mg/L). Check the unit, and that a thousands separator ('1,200') was not read as a decimal comma: write residuals without one.
files_refused.total_chlorine_column: The inlet residuals file's residual column, 'total_chlorine_mgL', is total chlorine, and the free-chlorine model reads free chlorine only: free and total chlorine are different measurements and one model never mixes them. Give each inlet's free chlorine residual.
files_refused.under_a_hundredth: The residual at Lake (0.005 mg/L) is less than a hundredth of the highest (River, 1.20 mg/L). Check its unit (mg/L; a µg/L value is 1000 times larger) and that a thousands separator ('1,200') was not read as a decimal comma.

ugl_file_notes: 2 residuals written with a decimal comma (0,45) were read as decimals (0.45).
The residual column 'Residual (ug/L)' is in µg/L (micrograms per litre): each residual was divided by 1000 to mg/L. Check that the unit is right.
